name: Standard scramble route
descent_text: The route is the trail, so you come down the way you went up. From the summit lookout, drop back through the rocky basin and the meadow, then follow the switchbacks down the shoulder, where the steep grade is hard on knees. Cross the avalanche chute again, take care on the loose rocky tread, and turn left at the junction onto the Pratt Lake trail for the last stretch to the trailhead. Round trip is roughly 8.6 miles with about 3,800 ft of gain. Snow cover, especially at the chute, turns this descent from a walk into a hazard.
approach: Start at the Pratt Lake trailhead at I-90 exit 47 and hike the Pratt Lake trail on moderate grade through forest. At about 1.2 miles a junction sends Granite Mountain Trail #1016 off to the right; Pratt Lake continues left. The Granite Mountain trail is the route, so the approach is simply the first miles of it: steep switchbacks, a crossing of a large avalanche chute just under a mile past the junction, then a traverse east onto the mountain's shoulder. In winter and early spring the chute is a real avalanche hazard.
